subject: maths
chapter_title: Orienting Yourself: The Use of Coordinates

concepts.title: The Coordinate Plane and Ordered Pairs
concepts.definition: The coordinate plane uses two perpendicular number lines - the x-axis and the y-axis - meeting at the origin; every location is written as an ordered pair (x, y) where x gives the horizontal shift and y the vertical, so coordinates give each point a unique address.
concepts.key_idea: Two numbers fix a place: walk x first along the horizontal, then y along the vertical.
concepts.textbook_ref: iemh101.txt sections 1.1-1.2 (introduction, settling in with coordinates)
question_patterns: write the coordinates of the given point on the plane
locate the point (3, 4) on the coordinate plane
which axis does the point (0, 5) lie on
what does the first number of an ordered pair tell
plot the given ordered pairs and name the shape formed
why are coordinates called an ordered pair

solution_steps.explain: Move along the horizontal axis by the first number.
Move parallel to the vertical axis by the second number.
The crossing of the two moves is the exact point.

compute_steps.action: recall the count for the shape
compute_steps.explain: recall the count for the shape: lines = 3 gives 3

concepts.title: Quadrants and Signs of Coordinates
concepts.definition: The axes divide the plane into four quadrants: in the first both coordinates are positive, in the second x is negative and y positive, in the third both are negative, and in the fourth x is positive and y negative; points on the axes have one coordinate zero.
concepts.key_idea: Signs reveal the address: the quadrant of a point is read from the signs of x and y.
question_patterns: in which quadrant does the point (-3, 5) lie
what are the signs of coordinates of points in the fourth quadrant
which points lie on the x-axis and why
write the coordinates of a point on the negative y-axis
name the quadrant for the given ordered pair
where does the origin lie and what are its coordinates

solution_steps.explain: Positive x puts the point to the right; negative to the left.
Positive y lifts the point up; negative pulls it down.
The two signs together fix one of the four quadrants or an axis.

compute_steps.explain: apply the coordinate-geometry formula: dx = 5 - -1 gives 6
apply the coordinate-geometry formula: dy = 3 - -5 gives 8
apply the coordinate-geometry formula: dist = sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy) gives 10

concepts.title: Distance Between Two Points
concepts.definition: The straight distance between points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) comes from the Pythagorean idea: square the horizontal gap and the vertical gap, add them, and take the square root.
concepts.key_idea: Horizontal and vertical gaps make the legs; the distance is the hypotenuse.
concepts.textbook_ref: iemh101.txt section 1.3 (use of coordinates for distances)
question_patterns: find the distance between the points (2, 3) and (6, 6)
calculate the distance of the point (5, 12) from the origin
find the distance between the two given points using coordinates
which of the two points is closer to the origin
show that the given triangle is right angled using distances
find a point at the given distance from another on the x-axis

solution_steps.explain: Compute the horizontal and vertical differences.
Square both gaps, add and take the square root.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Find the distance between the points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2).

solution_template.explain: Subtract the coordinates for the horizontal and vertical gaps.
Square, add, and take the square root.

solution_template.explain: Square, add and take the root for the distance.
